notes_endorse: Higher pay would help avoid corruption; we support this amendment

prop_desc: Constitutional amendments can be proposed only at regular biennial sessions of the legislature; this proposal would allow their passage at special sessions as well
notes_endorse: There seems to be no pressing need to increase the opportunity or decrease the time lag for proposing amendments; we oppose this amendment

prop_desc: Texas now pays its lieutenant governor and speaker of the House the same salary as state legislators; proposed amendment would increase salary of both to $22,500 per year
notes_endorse: Speaker should receive other compensation - apartments, staff money and the like; for these reasons, we oppose passage of this amendment

prop_desc: Texas currently prohibits anyone receiving a state salary from holding any public office; would allow state employees who are not state office-holders to serve as members of governing bodies of school districts, cities, towns or other local governmental districts without forfeiting their state salaries
notes_endorse: We believe its passage would be in the best interest of better local government - actually closer reading: editorial expresses concerns, says state law now prohibits teachers at state colleges from school board positions; final stance: we believe its passage would be in best interest

prop_desc: Texas Constitution currently limits interest which can be paid on bonds issued by the state to less than 5 percent in most cases; this amendment would allow setting of a 6 percent weighted average annual interest rate
notes_endorse: As a consequence, some state programs are finding the financial going tough; we support this amendment

prop_desc: Final proposed amendment is highly technical in nature; dating back to days of Republic of Texas, certain lands were set aside for each county for educational purposes; proposed amendment would allow the funds themselves to be tapped for buildings
notes_endorse: Since this would deplete the permanent funds and offer no replacement for them, we oppose this amendment

prop_desc: Demonstrates need for constitutional revision; would abolish the Lamar County Hospital District created by previous amendment
notes_endorse: Matter is strictly local in nature; we support its passage - actually editorial says we support, treating as endorsed

prop_desc: Some justices of the peace are still paid on a 'fee' instead of salary basis; would abolish the practice and require all justices to be paid by salary
notes_endorse: In the interest of better, fairer and more uniform justice and law enforcement, we support this amendment

prop_desc: Calls for establishment of a constitutional revision commission which would report its recommendations to the legislature no later than Nov 1, 1973; the legislature would convene in January 1974 as a constitutional convention to act upon those recommendations
notes_endorse: Needed task editorial - The Caller-Times supports the passage of Amendment 4 in the hope its passage can result in providing Texas with the constitutional reform it so badly needs

prop_desc: Constitutional revision commission and convention to rewrite the present constitution in its entirety
notes_endorse: We support Amendment 4 - the only one available now to advance constitutional revision

prop_desc: Grant to disabled veterans, surviving spouses and surviving minor children, and survivors of those killed on active duty, certain exemptions from property taxes (amount of exemption not to exceed $3,000)
notes_endorse: We oppose this amendment - says we believe it accomplished in other ways than by granting property tax relief - actually opposed

prop_desc: Allow but not require various political subdivisions (cities, school districts, hospital districts) to grant homestead exemption of not less than $3,000 on property taxes assessed persons 65 or older
notes_endorse: We do not believe this is the best way to go about it since the exemption would not take into account the person's need for such assistance; we oppose this amendment

prop_desc: Equal Rights Amendment - first proposed by women's rights advocates; the law shall not be denied or abridged because of sex, race, color, creed or national origin

notes_endorse: This question is dealt with in broader terms in Amendment 12; we oppose this amendment

prop_desc: Would double the capacity of the Texas Water Development Board to issue state bonds, adding an additional $400 million
notes_endorse: We do not believe this is necessary at this time; for this and environmental reasons, we recommend a vote against Amendment 1

prop_desc: Would approve the issuance of $100 million in bonds for water treatment facilities
notes_endorse: Since many communities in the state cannot, without the assistance of state loans, meet their water treatment needs, this bond capacity is vitally needed; we recommend a vote for Amendment 2

prop_desc: Tax Relief Amendment - omnibus property tax package including homestead exemption, productivity tax for agricultural land, equalized appraisals, and educational aid based on need
notes_endorse: We recommend a vote against the Tax Relief Amendment; voting against this amendment now is the best way to achieve the sort of tax relief Texas really wants

prop_desc: Permit the legislature to authorize banks to use unmanned teller machines for making deposits and cashing checks and other customer services
notes_endorse: Only the depositor could use the machine; we support No. 1

prop_desc: Grant the state the right of appeal from certain pretrial rulings in criminal cases
notes_endorse: We oppose this; would overload the appellate court system; entire criminal justice system would be jeopardized

prop_desc: Provide for a single appraisal unit in each county and a single equalization board in each county

prop_desc: Abolish the state ad valorem tax

prop_desc: Lift the unrealistic ceiling on the amount of state aid that can be matched with federal money for Aid to Families with Dependent Children (AFDC); current ceiling is $80 million
notes_endorse: Texas now provides only $34 per month in average benefits - ranking it 49th among the states; deals with controversial issue of welfare; passage is necessary to make Texas bonds saleable

prop_desc: Exempt agricultural machinery and equipment from ad valorem taxes; partnerships and corporations as well as individuals involved in farming would receive the exemption

prop_desc: Limit the terms of governing boards of certain water districts to four years, most now are limited to two years

prop_desc: Increase the maximum interest rate allowed on state general obligation bonds to 12 percent annually; current limit of 6 percent is grossly out of line with bond market reality
notes_endorse: Passage is necessary to make Texas bonds saleable

notes_endorse: This newspaper recommends a vote against only one of these, Amendment Two

prop_desc: Extending Officials' Terms - four-year terms for district, county and precinct officials including district clerks, county and district attorneys, county judges, judges of county courts at law, county clerks, county treasurers, county surveyors, sheriffs, assessors-collectors, county commissioners precincts 2 and 4, justices of the peace

prop_desc: Annual sessions for the Legislature and higher pay for legislators

prop_desc: Expand retirement, disability and death benefits for county employees and extend coverage to elected officials; separate county systems have too small a base to be actuarially sound

prop_desc: Provide that vacancies in county elective offices be filled only until the next general election, rather than for the longer periods now possible under the four-year terms created in 1954

prop_desc: Assess all property based on agricultural use rather than fair market value

prop_desc: Phase out the 35-cent state property-tax rate for schools by 1974 and end the 2-cent rate for state buildings in 1975; leaving only the state's 10-cent rate for college buildings
notes_endorse: We have long advocated that the state get out of the ad valorem tax field; ultimately we hope the state will abandon this tax source completely; this amendment would approach that goal

prop_desc: Repeal the requirement for the governor, comptroller and secretary of state to sign Board of Control contracts for state fuel and printing, a needless red-tape burden on busy officials

Authorize higher-paid public school teachers and college and university faculty members to contribute more (state-matched) for improved retirement pay; should help get and keep better educators in Texas institutions
notes_endorse: Three amendments are debatable but we doubt they would serve well their good intent - actually FOR per text

prop_desc: Provide a means for removal, retirement, or censure of justices, judges and justices of the peace - judicial reform
notes_endorse: Editorial endorses adoption of all 7 amendments

prop_desc: Repeal constitutional prohibition against open saloons; permit Legislature to regulate liquor by the drink on local option basis
Repeal the constitutional prohibition against open saloons; allow liquor by the drink on a local-option basis
notes_endorse: Yes on No. 2; the case for legalizing liquor by the drink in Texas is a case for straightforwardness and an end to hypocrisy; we can think of no stronger argument in support of a 'Yes' vote for Amendment No. 2

prop_desc: Authorize Legislature to provide by law for uniform method of assessing ranch, farm and forest lands based on productive capability
Reconstitute the State Building Commission as a three-member appointive commission
Permit any county, on vote of majority of qualified property taxpaying citizens, to issue road bonds up to one-fourth of assessed valuation of real property
Raise to $5,000 the present constitutional limit on a homestead exempt from forced sale and increase property costs
Authorize Legislature to provide for consolidation of governmental offices and functions and permit political subdivisions to contract for performance of governmental functions in any county
Increase salaries of state senators and representatives to $8,400 a year from present $4,800
notes_endorse: Higher pay would help avoid corruption; we support this amendment

prop_desc: Constitutional amendments can be proposed only at regular biennial sessions of the legislature; this proposal would allow their passage at special sessions as well
notes_endorse: There seems to be no pressing need to increase the opportunity or decrease the time lag for proposing amendments; we oppose this amendment

prop_desc: Texas now pays its lieutenant governor and speaker of the House the same salary as state legislators; proposed amendment would increase salary of both to $22,500 per year
notes_endorse: Speaker should receive other compensation - apartments, staff money and the like; for these reasons, we oppose passage of this amendment

prop_desc: Texas currently prohibits anyone receiving a state salary from holding any public office; would allow state employees who are not state office-holders to serve as members of governing bodies of school districts, cities, towns or other local governmental districts without forfeiting their state salaries
notes_endorse: We believe its passage would be in the best interest of better local government - actually closer reading: editorial expresses concerns, says state law now prohibits teachers at state colleges from school board positions; final stance: we believe its passage would be in best interest

prop_desc: Texas Constitution currently limits interest which can be paid on bonds issued by the state to less than 5 percent in most cases; this amendment would allow setting of a 6 percent weighted average annual interest rate
notes_endorse: As a consequence, some state programs are finding the financial going tough; we support this amendment

prop_desc: Final proposed amendment is highly technical in nature; dating back to days of Republic of Texas, certain lands were set aside for each county for educational purposes; proposed amendment would allow the funds themselves to be tapped for buildings
notes_endorse: Since this would deplete the permanent funds and offer no replacement for them, we oppose this amendment

prop_desc: Demonstrates need for constitutional revision; would abolish the Lamar County Hospital District created by previous amendment
notes_endorse: Matter is strictly local in nature; we support its passage - actually editorial says we support, treating as endorsed

prop_desc: Some justices of the peace are still paid on a 'fee' instead of salary basis; would abolish the practice and require all justices to be paid by salary
notes_endorse: In the interest of better, fairer and more uniform justice and law enforcement, we support this amendment

prop_desc: Calls for establishment of a constitutional revision commission which would report its recommendations to the legislature no later than Nov 1, 1973; the legislature would convene in January 1974 as a constitutional convention to act upon those recommendations
notes_endorse: Needed task editorial - The Caller-Times supports the passage of Amendment 4 in the hope its passage can result in providing Texas with the constitutional reform it so badly needs

prop_desc: Constitutional revision commission and convention to rewrite the present constitution in its entirety
notes_endorse: We support Amendment 4 - the only one available now to advance constitutional revision

prop_desc: Grant to disabled veterans, surviving spouses and surviving minor children, and survivors of those killed on active duty, certain exemptions from property taxes (amount of exemption not to exceed $3,000)
notes_endorse: We oppose this amendment - says we believe it accomplished in other ways than by granting property tax relief - actually opposed

prop_desc: Allow but not require various political subdivisions (cities, school districts, hospital districts) to grant homestead exemption of not less than $3,000 on property taxes assessed persons 65 or older
notes_endorse: We do not believe this is the best way to go about it since the exemption would not take into account the person's need for such assistance; we oppose this amendment

prop_desc: Equal Rights Amendment - first proposed by women's rights advocates; the law shall not be denied or abridged because of sex, race, color, creed or national origin

Increase terms of the governor, lieutenant governor, attorney general, comptroller of public accounts, treasurer, commissioner of the General Land Office, secretary of state and other statutory state officers from two to four years
Proposal deals only with directors of soil and water conservation districts; would permit them to simultaneously hold and be compensated for other public office
notes_endorse: This question is dealt with in broader terms in Amendment 12; we oppose this amendment

prop_desc: Would double the capacity of the Texas Water Development Board to issue state bonds, adding an additional $400 million
notes_endorse: We do not believe this is necessary at this time; for this and environmental reasons, we recommend a vote against Amendment 1

prop_desc: Would approve the issuance of $100 million in bonds for water treatment facilities
notes_endorse: Since many communities in the state cannot, without the assistance of state loans, meet their water treatment needs, this bond capacity is vitally needed; we recommend a vote for Amendment 2

prop_desc: Tax Relief Amendment - omnibus property tax package including homestead exemption, productivity tax for agricultural land, equalized appraisals, and educational aid based on need
notes_endorse: We recommend a vote against the Tax Relief Amendment; voting against this amendment now is the best way to achieve the sort of tax relief Texas really wants

prop_desc: Permit the legislature to authorize banks to use unmanned teller machines for making deposits and cashing checks and other customer services
notes_endorse: Only the depositor could use the machine; we support No. 1

prop_desc: Grant the state the right of appeal from certain pretrial rulings in criminal cases
notes_endorse: We oppose this; would overload the appellate court system; entire criminal justice system would be jeopardized

prop_desc: Provide for a single appraisal unit in each county and a single equalization board in each county
notes_endorse: Further step in making the state's taxing system fairer and more equitable; should be approved by the voters

prop_desc: Authorize legalization of bingo for charitable purposes on a local option basis
Authorize the legislature to give budget execution power to the governor, subject to approval by a budget execution committee; move toward more business-like management of appropriated funds
Authorize the governor to remove state officials he has appointed with advice and consent of Senate
Permit counties with a population of 5,000 or less to perform private road work if a reasonable charge is imposed
notes_endorse: Such an amendment, it seems to us, is not needed; opens the door for all kinds of abuse; we oppose it

prop_desc: Change the name of the 14 Courts of Civil Appeals to Courts of Appeal and give those courts jurisdiction in criminal cases as well as civil cases; relieve Court of Criminal Appeals workload
Authorize the conversion of certain marital community property into separate property by allowing spouses to agree that income from separate property is to be separate property
notes_endorse: Changes this would permit in Texas community property laws, in our opinion, would be too broad; we oppose this amendment

prop_desc: Abolish the state ad valorem tax
notes_endorse: Should please most everyone; in reality, that tax has not been collected since 1980, when the Legislature lowered the rate so drastically as to make collecting it unprofitable; must be stricken from the constitution to satisfy legal requirements

prop_desc: Lift the unrealistic ceiling on the amount of state aid that can be matched with federal money for Aid to Families with Dependent Children (AFDC); current ceiling is $80 million
notes_endorse: Texas now provides only $34 per month in average benefits - ranking it 49th among the states; deals with controversial issue of welfare; passage is necessary to make Texas bonds saleable

prop_desc: Exempt agricultural machinery and equipment from ad valorem taxes; partnerships and corporations as well as individuals involved in farming would receive the exemption
notes_endorse: No organized opposition; both Democratic and Republican candidates for agriculture commissioner support amendment

prop_desc: Limit the terms of governing boards of certain water districts to four years, most now are limited to two years
notes_endorse: We can see no harm resulting from its passage

prop_desc: Permit abolishing of the offices of county treasurer in Bee and Tarrant (Fort Worth) counties, shifting duties to the county auditor, if voters in those counties approve
notes_endorse: Allowing Bee and Tarrant voters to eliminate the office in their counties would at least provide the state with a laboratory test

prop_desc: Increase the maximum interest rate allowed on state general obligation bonds to 12 percent annually; current limit of 6 percent is grossly out of line with bond market reality
notes_endorse: Passage is necessary to make Texas bonds saleable

prop_desc: Six proposed constitutional amendments on Tuesday's ballot
Would end the constitutional requirement that bills before the Legislature be correctly captioned, making that instead a subject of legislative rules
notes_endorse: This newspaper recommends a vote against only one of these, Amendment Two

prop_desc: $2.4 million Nueces County bond proposal to finance a new 24-bed juvenile detention building at Martineau Juvenile Hall
Bond issue 2000 - $58.8 million in bonds for Propositions 1, 2, and 3 (parks, recreation centers, neighborhood parks, dog and animal pound, and fire stations)
Prop. 1: Continuation of Crime Control District
Prop. 2: New and expanded business enterprises
Proposed Constitutional Amendment - Giving Texas counties the right to declare constables' offices 'dormant' if they have not been filled for seven years
CCISD bond - $194 million for school consolidations, replacement campuses and upgrades
City Proposition 12: Bond election - $18 million for residential streets and other amenities
City Proposition 1: Type B economic development sales tax
City Proposition 2: Continuation of expiring Crime Control District
City Proposition 3: Residential street reconstruction tax
Del Mar bond - $139 million for Southside campus
Corpus Christi City bond - $96 million, six separate proposals for street work, public safety, public health department building, parks and libraries
Corpus Christi ISD bond - $210,770,000 for new Carroll High School, gyms and other construction, security upgrades, technology upgrades

Medical Amendment - state fund to send medical school graduates to college and require them after graduation to practice a specified time in rural areas where doctor-service is lacking; on Nov. 4 ballot
notes_endorse: Editorial opposes; says it puts the state into medicine; calls subsidizing professionals 'socialism'; says it isn't the answer to admittedly serious problem

prop_desc: Old Age Amendment - Senate Joint Resolution No. 7; would authorize Legislature to increase spending for old age assistance, aid to blind, aid to dependent children by $7 million a year; would raise ceiling to $42 million; require recipient names be made public
notes_endorse: Editorial raises significant concerns; argues real need is restudy of eligibility requirements so those who don't really need can be taken off rolls; Texas already has 38 percent or twice the national deadwood; lean against passage

prop_desc: Toll Road Amendment - would prohibit the use of the credit of the state or grant of any public money for construction, maintenance or operation of toll roads and turnpikes
notes_endorse: Editorial says amendment is unwise and unnecessary; tying hands of state appears unwise; appears to have the least merit of all 11 amendments

prop_desc: Extending Officials' Terms - four-year terms for district, county and precinct officials (district clerks, county and district attorneys, county judges, county clerks, county treasurers, sheriffs, county commissioners precincts 2 and 4, justices of the peace)
notes_endorse: Editorial favors extension; calls it a sound measure giving greater job stability and promoting efficiency and public service; notes adoption is doubtful due to controversy

prop_desc: Building Amendment - creates a State Building Commission with authority to erect buildings for state use; would transfer surplus from Confederate Pension Fund (~$6 million) to this purpose
notes_endorse: Building Amendment Should Be Adopted; no opposition heard; should most certainly be approved; provides roundabout solution to a pressing problem

prop_desc: Annexation of area south and west of present city limits of Corpus Christi (local referendum)
notes_endorse: Vote Today editorial says annexation can only fail to pass if Corpus Christi voters fail to go to the polls; advantages outweigh disadvantages; vital to future healthy growth of the city

prop_desc: Annual session for the Legislature and higher pay for legislators (raise to $7,500 annual salary)
notes_endorse: Editorial says Vote No on Amendment No. 1; says language likely cause more ills than it would cure

prop_desc: Would expand retirement, disability and death benefits for county employees and extend coverage to elected officials
Would provide that vacancies in county elective offices be filled only until the next general election rather than for the longer periods now possible under the four-year terms created in 1954
notes_endorse: Recommendation: Yes - technical but important adjustment

prop_desc: Would correct difficulty caused by new four-year county terms; would require district, county and precinct officials with more than a year of their term remaining to resign on announcing their candidacy for any other office
notes_endorse: Recommendation: No - though purpose is being defeated by those who hold onto one office while running for another

prop_desc: Would provide pensions for Rangers who retired before becoming eligible for regular state employee pensions
notes_endorse: Recommendation: No - amendment is not favored by the Texas Department of Public Safety

prop_desc: Would remove Texas' unique anachronistic constitutional ban on state advertising; would establish a state advertising program in Texas Department of Commerce
Would authorize state vending of federal funds for payment direct to vendor of medical services accorded recipients of federal-state welfare assistance
notes_endorse: Recommendation: No - estimated cost of nine million dollars a year would be only the beginning; administrative difficulties are formidable

prop_desc: Would permit four more taxing hospital districts; a local-option authority granted in 1954 to counties of more than 190,000 population; in lieu of a preferable general and uniform constitutional permission
notes_endorse: Recommendation: Yes - implemented by legislation as necessary, such projects as these should be allowed despite obvious tendency toward a hodgepodge system

prop_desc: County Home Rule amendment - would give counties same powers of home rule as cities enjoy; proposed by Harris County Home-Rule Commission; would also allow optional city-county consolidation
notes_endorse: Editorial strongly urges local support for the statewide county home-rule movement; insists Nueces County be included in any such grant of county home-rule authority
Editorial recommends voter consider each and vote his best judgment; Proposal No. 1 would allow workman's compensation insurance; recommended voter look against
Editorial: Of the other dozen amendment proposals, none appears either urgently necessary or seriously objectionable; recommended that the voter consider each and vote his best judgment

prop_desc: Would allow workmen's compensation insurance amendment
notes_endorse: Editorial mentioned but no clear recommendation; Of the other dozen amendment proposals, none appears either urgently necessary or seriously objectionable

prop_desc: Would allow state employees, with superior's permission, to be paid for consulting or advisory services to other state agencies and political subdivisions
notes_endorse: Editorial: This should allow for better use of talent without any serious risk of conflict of interest

prop_desc: Would allow state employees, with superior's permission, to be used for consulting or advisory services to other state agencies and political subdivisions
notes_endorse: Editorial: This should allow for better use of talent without any serious risk of conflict of interest - though phrasing suggests the editorial leans against; ambiguous

prop_desc: Would allow resale of lands in the Veterans Land Fund to nonveterans, provided such repossessed land has been unsuccessfully offered for resale to veterans

Of special interest to Nueces County and the Coastal Bend area generally; would allow the legislature to authorize coastal counties to regulate speed limits and prevent litter on public beaches; private property zoning is not involved
notes_endorse: Editorial: We believe this amendment is a good one and should be adopted

prop_desc: School district consolidation; technicality applicable and of interest only to Dallas County
notes_endorse: Editorial: Whether you vote on the constitutional amendment proposals or not will not affect the validity of the rest of your ballot - no recommendation

prop_desc: Would have state courts review appeals from administrative decisions of state agencies, cities, counties, school and special districts; would seriously impair efficiency and fairness of administration of state and local government
notes_endorse: Editorial: 'Vote FOR Four—and AGAINST Fourteen'; would cripple local government; unnecessary, unwise and even dangerous attempt by the legislature to interfere in state administration, judicial review and home-rule local government

prop_desc: Would rule local government in water conservation matters
notes_endorse: Editorial slogan 'Vote FOR Four—and AGAINST Fourteen'; would cripple local government

prop_desc: Would raise the ceiling on aid to needy aged, needy blind and dependent children from $47 million to $52 million annually
notes_endorse: Editorial supports raising ceilings as state's population and social problems have grown

prop_desc: Would raise the ceiling on aid to totally and permanently disabled persons from $1.5 million to $2.5 million annually; raise welfare ceilings as state's population and social problems have grown
notes_endorse: Texas voters have, by constitutional amendment, approved 16 hospital districts since 1954; ceilings have had to be raised from time to time as state's population grown

prop_desc: Would authorize four more hospital districts (including in northeast Texas)
notes_endorse: Editorial supports continuation of hospital district approach; would avoid cumbersome process

prop_desc: Would authorize the legislature to authorize hospital districts by statute subject to local-option election; two more in northeast Texas and two in Brazoria County
notes_endorse: Editorial supports continuation of hospital district approach

prop_desc: Would raise the ceiling on aid to totally and permanently disabled persons from $1.5 to $2.5 million annually; welfare ceilings raised as state's population and social problems have grown
notes_endorse: Editorial supports raising ceilings as state's population and social problems have grown

prop_desc: Would authorize the state to use bond money to participate in federal and/or local dam projects to accelerate development of the state's water resource sites; build or design dams higher and acquire more reservoir right-of-way than immediately needed
notes_endorse: Editorial slogan 'Vote FOR Four—and AGAINST Fourteen'; this authority overdue to prevent underfunding of dams and wasting of limited and precious reservoir potentials; substantially stimulated; highly recommended

prop_desc: Would authorize four more hospital districts (two more in northeast Texas and two in Brazoria County); would end the cumbersome process by allowing the legislature to authorize hospital districts by statute subject to local-option election
notes_endorse: Editorial supports continuation of hospital district approach

prop_desc: Would authorize four more hospital districts in Brazoria County
notes_endorse: Editorial supports hospital district expansion through these proposals

prop_desc: Would make elective officials of certain and other political subdivisions eligible for retirement plans, as appointive officers and employees provide for local option
notes_endorse: Editorial supports - both of the amendments provide for local option

prop_desc: Would make elective officials of counties and other political subdivisions eligible for retirement plans, as appointive officers and employees; provide for local option
notes_endorse: Editorial supports - both of the amendments provide for local option

prop_desc: Would authorize the legislature to provide for war disaster lines of succession to appointive and elective offices of state and local government, except for the governor; emergency caused by enemy attack
notes_endorse: Editorial supports as a reasonable defense measure applicable only to emergency caused by enemy attack

prop_desc: Would have state courts review appeals from administrative decisions of state agencies, cities, counties, school and special districts on the basis of whether those decisions or rulings are constitutional, within statutory authority, reasonable and based on substantial evidence
notes_endorse: Editorial: unnecessary, unwise and even dangerous attempt by the legislature to interfere in state administration, judicial review and home-rule local government

prop_desc: Would twice raise the ceiling on state funds for aiding the needy aged, needy blind and dependent children from $47 million to $52 million annually
notes_endorse: Editorial supports raising ceilings as state's population and social problems have grown

prop_desc: Would repeal an unwise constitutional amendment approved in 1891 that now allows the Legislature to transfer up to 1 per cent of the capital in the Permanent School Fund in any one year to the available School Fund for current state-aid school expenses; would protect the $335 million Permanent School Fund
notes_endorse: Editorial 'Amendment Proposals': urge all Texans concerned for the long-range development of their public school system to vote for it; Voting for Amendment No. 1 will assure maximum benefit both to Texas taxpayers and Texas school children from this state's unique public school endowment

prop_desc: Would assess all property taxation on individually owned farm and ranch land on the basis of its agricultural uses, rather than by the fair market rate now applying to all land; favored by Texas Farm Bureau, opposed by Texas Municipal League
notes_endorse: Editorial 'The Amendments': 'Vote AGAINST amendments No. 1 and No. 7. Vote FOR all the rest.' Recommended vote: AGAINST

prop_desc: Would allow expansion of boundaries, or merger, of school and junior college districts without requiring an election

Would allow the expansion of boundaries, or merger, of school and junior college districts without requiring an election to receive tax rates and validate unissued bonds; Dallas County already has this freedom
notes_endorse: Recommended vote: FOR. It should be made statewide

prop_desc: Greatly important and highly desirable, especially favorable to South Texas; would double the revolving State Water Development Fund to $400 million, with a two-thirds vote of the Legislature required to issue any or all of the additional bonds; bond funds are lent to local governments for water projects
notes_endorse: Recommended vote: FOR. This type of financing is indispensable if the state is not to forfeit control of its essential water development to the federal government

prop_desc: Would double the revolving State Water Development Fund to $400 million for water projects
notes_endorse: Recommended vote: FOR. Greatly important and highly desirable, especially favorable to South Texas

prop_desc: Would double the revolving State Water Development Fund to $400 million; bond funds are lent to local governments for water projects
notes_endorse: Recommended vote: FOR. Greatly important and highly desirable, especially favorable to South Texas

prop_desc: Would authorize the Legislature to provide for dissolution of hospital districts it is now constitutionally empowered to create; would correct a legal oversight that now prevents a county from getting rid of a hospital district it no longer wants
Would allow local-option consolidation of local governments in Harris County
Would allow local-option consolidation of local governments in Harris County and permit service contracts among them

Would, in effect, allow local-option consolidation of local governments in Harris County and permit service contracts among them; The authority should be statewide, but we see no reason why the Houston area should not make an experimental start on rationalizing the metropolitan-area governmental hodgepodge

Would repeal state constitutional restrictions on military service personnel acquiring residence anywhere in Texas for voting purposes; would merely adjust the constitutional wording to conform to a 1965 U.S. Supreme Court decision that is now the ruling law

Would allow state, federal and private funds for rehabilitation and vocational training of the physically or mentally handicapped to be consolidated under the State Board of Education, applying state auditing controls; would provide a way for private contributions to be matched by federal funds under the federal vocational training law
notes_endorse: Recommended vote: FOR. This would increase urgently needed aid and give more central direction for coping with a statewide problem

prop_desc: Would consolidate state, federal and private funds for rehabilitation and vocational training of physically or mentally handicapped under the State Board of Education

Would specify that terms of all members of the Texas Legislature begin on Jan. 2 after their election; would simply clarify an ambiguity in the original constitution that has caused confusion and pay problems for many years and is now interpreted as starting senators' terms on election day and representatives' terms when returns are made official around Nov. 20
Would authorize local voters to create a taxing airport authority in one or more counties; designed to help Dallas and Fort Worth build a regional airport for the unique twin-city area
notes_endorse: Recommended vote: FOR. We see no reason for South Texans to oppose that

prop_desc: Would complete the transfer of Arlington State College from the Texas A&M University System to the University of Texas System
Would merely complete the transfer of Arlington State College from the Texas A&M University System to the University of Texas System
Would authorize six-year staggered terms for all conservation and reclamation district directors, some of which are now limited to two-year terms
notes_endorse: Recommended vote: FOR. This would allow uniformity and clarify a legally confused situation

prop_desc: Would authorize the Legislature to set up a statewide cooperative system of retirement, disability and death benefits for employees of counties and other political subdivisions; participation would be at local option, locally financed
Would authorize the Legislature to provide assistance payments to widows and children of law-enforcement officers, full-time firemen, and prison guards killed in line of duty
Would 'repeal the poll tax as a requirement for voting'
notes_endorse: Recommended vote: AGAINST. Editorial: 'Vote AGAINST amendments No. 1 and No. 7'

prop_desc: Would 'repeal the poll tax as a requirement for voting,' which is unnecessary as the U.S. Supreme Court has already invalidated that requirement; needless amendment as poll-tax list be replaced by an annual registration system
notes_endorse: Recommended vote: AGAINST. Editorial: 'Vote AGAINST amendments No. 1 and No. 7'; Legislature should be free to adopt a permanent registration system safeguarded against fraud to encourage maximum voter turnout

prop_desc: Would end temporary disenfranchisement in presidential and state elections of Texans moving within the state and in presidential elections of voters moving from other states to Texas
Would end temporary disenfranchisement of Texans moving within the state and presidential election voters moving to or from Texas

Would end the temporary disenfranchisement in presidential and state elections of Texans moving within the state who fail to meet county and precinct residential requirements, and in presidential elections only of voters moving from other states to Texas or to other states
notes_endorse: Recommended vote: FOR. It would remove undemocratic restrictions on otherwise eligible voters

prop_desc: Would increase the Texas Court of Criminal Appeals from three to five judges
Would increase the Texas Court of Criminal Appeals from three to five judges, by making judges of two commissioners who now serve as judges without a vote on decisions
notes_endorse: Recommended vote: FOR. The court's work load justifies this expansion

prop_desc: New York state constitutional amendment to adopt a state revenue-producing lottery on Nov. 8 election; revenue would benefit education
notes_endorse: Editorial 'Wrong Way': we hope the proposal fails; would not like to see the idea spread; government lottery gives an official condonation to gambling likely to produce a climate nourishing to all the criminal elements that prey on the gambling weakness; a shoddy and damaging way for a society to raise money

prop_desc: Would increase 50,000 state employes' contributions, matched by the state, as well as allow more investment in private securities, to provide higher retirement pay (state employes' retirement fund)
notes_endorse: Editorial 'Constitutional Amendment Recommendations Offered': State funds - we favor the three amendments considered desirable to increase income and improve management for the state universities' endowment, state employes' retirement fund and public school and college teachers' retirement fund; We believe to invest prudently for higher income for permanent improvements

prop_desc: Would exempt Texarkana, Texas from tobacco taxes so their merchants could compete better with those less taxed in Texarkana, Arkansas
notes_endorse: Editorial: Local Issues - lacks merit and should be a dubious precedent

prop_desc: Would let El Paso and Tarrant Counties integrate local government units, a metropolitan-area reform needed statewide
notes_endorse: Editorial: Local Issues - offers a worthwhile experiment

prop_desc: Would allow cities, counties and navigation districts to issue bonds, with interest exempt from federal income taxation, to buy sites and build plants for industry; offered to meet the industrialization competition of 44 states with such plans
notes_endorse: Editorial: Business aids - this stimulus to industrialization is not great, the device is being so widely abused that the federal government is likely soon to invalidate it, and government bond-financing potential should be reserved for urgently needed public projects

prop_desc: Would exempt for property taxation merchandise in warehouses awaiting out-of-state shipment on Jan. 1 (the assessment date)
notes_endorse: Editorial: Business aids - seems a minor business aid subject to abuse

prop_desc: Would reasonably let legislators run for other public offices whose terms would overlap only a few days
notes_endorse: Editorial: Clarifications - Both should be approved

prop_desc: Would increase from $60 million to $75 million the ceiling on the state's contribution to federal aid for needy aged (not under Social Security), the permanently disabled, the blind, and indigent parents (mostly mothers) of dependent children
notes_endorse: Editorial 'Three Major Amendments Deserve Voters' Approval': among the 14 state constitutional amendment proposals, three stand out as of exceptional statewide importance; recommendation that voters approve all three; voters are urged to study them, and we believe the majority will agree they should be approved

prop_desc: Would raise the state-aid ceiling on federal public welfare programs
notes_endorse: Editorial: This newspaper has already endorsed the three most important - Amendment No. 2 to raise the state-aid ceiling on federal public welfare programs

prop_desc: Would allow the regents of the University of Texas System and Texas A&M University System, which share Permanent University Fund's income, to investment more in corporate securities and less in government bonds
notes_endorse: Editorial: We favor the three amendments considered desirable; the fund managers can be trusted

prop_desc: Would allow Dallas County to issue road bonds by simple, rather than two-thirds, majority vote
notes_endorse: Editorial: Local Issues - majority vote is desired there and should be approved

prop_desc: Would raise state senators' and representatives' salaries from $4,800 a year to $8,400, with a modest increase in expenses and travel allowances; legislative service is now virtually a full-time job and should be compensated accordingly
notes_endorse: Editorial 'Three Major Amendments Deserve Voters' Approval': pay increase should attract better men and women into this important work, including those who cannot now afford the financial sacrifice of serving

prop_desc: Would let the Legislature exempt from state and local property taxation all equipment installed by industry to reduce air and water pollution; industry is allowed a federal tax deductible for state and local taxes, so it would be better for a tax incentive for this urgent purpose to be applied at the federal level
notes_endorse: Editorial: Business aids - this amendment would cost local governments revenue; the undrafted enabling legislation could have inequitable loopholes, and other states' experience cast doubt on its effectiveness

prop_desc: Would phase out the 35-cent state property-tax rate for schools by 1974 and end the 2-cent rate for state buildings in 1975, leaving only the state's 10-cent rate for college buildings; would have state get out of the ad valorem tax field
notes_endorse: Editorial 'Three Major Amendments Deserve Voters' Approval': we hope the state will abandon this tax source completely; this amendment would approach that goal
Editorial: Already endorsed by this newspaper

prop_desc: Would repeal the requirement for the governor, comptroller and secretary of state to sign Board of Control contracts for state fuel and printing, a needless red-tape burden on busy officials
notes_endorse: Editorial: Clarifications - Both should be approved

prop_desc: Would authorize higher-paid public school teachers and college and university faculty members to contribute more (state-matched) for improved retirement pay; this should help get and keep better educators in Texas institutions
notes_endorse: Editorial: State funds - we favor the three amendments considered desirable

prop_desc: Raise the permissable tax rate of the Nueces County Hospital District to a maximum of 75 cents on each $100 valuation from the present rate of 40 cents
notes_endorse: Editorial 'Need Is Obvious': we must take care of the hospital and medical needs of our indigent citizens because it is the right thing to do; voters can express their concern by an affirmative vote for change in financing and administration of the hospital district Tuesday

prop_desc: Replace the administration of Memorial Medical Center by the Nueces County Commissioners Court to an appointive board of citizens
notes_endorse: Editorial 'Need Is Obvious': it was a mistake to make the Commissioners Court the administrative head of the hospital district and Memorial Medical Center; this exposed the hospital to charges of 'politics'; some doctors predict this unfavorable climate will be changed almost overnight if the hospital is administered by a civilian board

prop_desc: Would provide a means for removal, retirement, or censure of justices, judges and justices of the peace; tentative but significant step toward fuller judicial reform
notes_endorse: Editorial 'The Amendments': We find substantial merit in all of the seven proposed constitutional amendments and urge their adoption by voters
